headline: Evidence-linked memory reduces memory-induced failures in reported agent benchmarks
summary: A new arXiv paper introduces WikiTrace, which links each agent-memory lesson to a diagnosis and the raw trajectory it came from, allowing an agent to revisit the source when a lesson is uncertain or conflicts with another. Across eight suites in five benchmarks, the authors report a mean score of 90.2, compared with 79.5 without memory and 87.0 for a matched baseline given the same insights without their source runs. Reported memory-induced Regression is 4.5% versus 6.5% for the matched baseline. These are author-run results under review, not an independent reproduction; most tests use simulated environments and the paper notes that source links do not themselves verify a lesson.
